metadata.description: Supplemental host-plant evidence extracted from PDFs retrieved after the GPT-Pro seed was generated.
sources: Muriel, S. B., Montoya, J., Restrepo, A. & Munoz, J. 2011. Nuevos registros de plantas hospederas y disponibilidad de recursos para mariposas Ithomiini, en agroecosistemas de cafe colombianos. Actualidades Biologicas 33(95): 275-285. DOI: 10.17533/udea.acbi.14326.
McClure, M. & Elias, M. 2016. Unravelling the role of host plant expansion in the diversification of a Neotropical butterfly genus. BMC Evolutionary Biology 16:128. DOI: 10.1186/s12862-016-0701-5.
notes: Muriel et al. Table 3 records are field-collected eggs/larvae/pupae reared in the laboratory from coffee agroecosystems in Fredonia, Antioquia, Colombia.
McClure & Elias records summarize field host-use context reported for the four Melinaea species studied; experimental host-acceptance-only results are not added as default host associations here.

records.evidence_type: field-collected immature stages reared in laboratory; Colombia host record
records.source_citation: Muriel et al. 2011, Actualidades Biologicas 33(95): 275-285, Table 3
records.source_refs: Fredonia, Antioquia, Colombia: Finca Santa Isabel, 1830 m; marked XX = new host-plant record for the Lepidoptera species in Colombia.
records.caveats: Local Colombian agroecosystem record; occurrence of the plant does not imply host use outside the sampled context.

records.evidence_type: field host-use context summarized before oviposition/performance experiment
records.source_refs: The paper reports previous surveys in northeastern Peru found all study Melinaea species use Juanulloa parasitica except M. mothone.
records.caveats: Source summarizes prior host-use context and then uses this plant in preference/performance experiments.

records.evidence_type: field host-use context and oviposition/performance experiment
records.source_refs: The paper reports M. mothone uses the novel host plant Trianaea speciosa in northeastern Peru and was the only study species collected from this host.
records.caveats: The same paper found M. mothone retained laboratory ability to use Juanulloa parasitica, but that lab-only potential host is not added as a default association.
